manifest.name: mattpocock-skills-dsh
manifest.description: Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity agent skills, packaged as a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. 27 skills from mattpocock/skills 1.3.2: grilling, spec and ticket flows, TDD, code review, domain modelling, and more.

bundle.text:
# mattpocock-skills-dsh bundle patch: mount one skill provider row into the
# host skill registry. Host-plane rows merge into every agent preset's scope
# chain, so all presets in the profile see these skills.
- insert:
    - id: mattpocock-skills-dsh
      name: 'mattpocock-skills-dsh'

readme.text: [Matt Pocock](https://www.aihero.dev)'s engineering and productivity agent skills, packaged as a plugin for the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**.

27 skills — grilling, spec and ticket flows, TDD, code review, domain modelling, and more — installed as one bundle. The skill bodies are **verbatim** from upstream [`mattpocock/skills`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) v1.3.2. Only the packaging is new: a Cordis plugin that registers a skill provider on `ctx.skills`, so every agent preset in a profile sees these skills.
The skills are "plug-and-play, not vibe coding": small, composable, and meant to be edited. Fork them and make them your own.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zhikedan/mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

Restart the Harness afterwards — a profile bundle is read at boot, so the skills appear in the next process, not the running one.

From a local checkout instead of GitHub:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add E:\path\to\mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

Remove it again:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

27 skills. `model + user` means the agent may reach for the skill on its own; `user only` means it is invoked by you, because upstream marks those flows `disable-model-invocation: true` — a prescribed sequence that should not fire by itself.

| Skill | Invocation | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ask-matt` | user only | Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. |
| `code-review` | model + user | Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". |
| `codebase-design` | model + user | Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary. |
| `diagnosing-bugs` | model + user | Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. |
| `domain-modeling` | model + user | Build and sharpen a project's domain model. U

```
package.json        bundle manifest — dsh.bundle.patch is what makes this a DSH bundle
dsh.plugin.json     plugin identity, engine range, and the contributed skill names
cordis.patch.yml    inserts the provider row into the host plane
lib/index.js        the Cordis plugin: skill provider protocol over skills/

The provider scans `skills/` one level deep, reads each `SKILL.md`'s YAML frontmatter for `name` and `description`, and loads the body only when a skill is actually requested. Each skill advertises a directory `resourceBase`, so a relative reference inside a body — [tests.md](skills/tdd/tests.md), `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` — resolves for the reader.
Bodies are byte-for-byte upstream; nothing is translated or rewritten. Four deliberate packaging differences:

1. **Flat skill directories.** Upstream groups skills into `skills/engineering/…` and `skills/productivity/…`. This package ships `skills/<name>/`, the layout the provider scans. `scripts/sync-skills.mjs` performs the flattening from upstream's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` skill list, so the promoted set stays upstream's decision.
2. **No `agents/openai.yaml`.** Those files are hints for another harness. Every `SKILL.md` and every relative reference it names is shipped.
3. **Invocation mapping.** Upstream's `disable-model-invocation: true` becomes `invocation.modelInvocable: false`, so a user-invoked flow stays user-invoked instead of becoming an auto-trigger.
4. **Rank 550.** Below the bundled root's 600, so a harness-shipped skill of the same name always wins. A plugin must not shadow the host.
`retro`, `pr` and `implement-spec` are part of upstream's promoted set and are included; the unpromoted `in-progress/`, `misc/`, and `deprecated/` buckets are not.

```powershell
node scripts/check.mjs             # contract check, exit 1 on any violation
node scripts/check.mjs --markdown  # same checks, plus the table above
```

The check loads `lib/index.js` through the export shape Cordis reads, replays the registry's own validation over every candidate and definition (name pattern, non-empty description, boolean invocation flags, provider identity, finite rank, directory resource base), resolves every relative reference each body names, and confirms `dsh.plugin.json`, `package.json`, and the provider agree on the skill set. What it cannot prove is runtime presentation: the skill catalog a session sees, and the Plugin Manager row, need a Harness restart to observe.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/mattpocock/skills
node scripts/sync-skills.mjs .\skills
node scripts/check.mjs
```

Then set `version` in both `package.json` and `dsh.plugin.json` to the upstream version, and update `contributes.skills` if the promoted set changed. The check fails when the manifests and the provider disagree, so a missed edit cannot ship silently.
